candidates.structural_interaction: Earth generating Metal same-polarity — stability as natural source of precision
candidates.k2_overview: Your Metal moves as the Artisan: an edge that makes beautiful, useful things instead of wounds. Craft flows out of you calmly, finished on the first pass more often than seems fair. You feed people with precision, the perfectly chosen gift, the exact right word, and your pleasure runs quiet and specific.
candidates.k2_functional: You say precise, kind things that people keep. Your compliments are engraved, not sprayed.

k2_domain_readings.Expression: Your expression is craftsmanship: things made exactly, words placed cleanly, taste visible in every output. You do not need volume. One finished piece says what an hour of talk cannot, so keep finishing pieces.
k2_domain_readings.Enjoyment: You enjoy like a connoisseur of the specific: the correct knife, the true note, the single well-made thing. Fund those pleasures without guilt. Precision delight is how this energy refuels its edge.
k2_domain_readings.Children: With children and the people you mentor, you teach by craft: hands shown, tools trusted early, standards kept warm. What they inherit from you is the quiet confidence of making things properly.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, little leaves the gate. What does leave has to be worth it, and your care goes into the few pieces you let go.

angles.drive: You love the craft for its own sake, whatever the thing you are making. Shaping something with care is where you feel most at home, and the hours pass without your counting them. What you make shows that it was enjoyed in the making.
angles.cost_self: Loving the craft draws you back to the work above almost anything else. You need part of every day to go into making something, and other plans wait their turn. Friends and sleep get whatever evenings the craft leaves over.
angles.cost_others: The people around you often find you deep in a piece of work. Losing yourself in the making is your favourite way to be, and a question from the doorway takes a moment to reach you. Your family shares you with the craft.

angles.drive: Choosing the right thing to give is how you care. A wrong gift feels worse to you than none, so you choose slowly rather than give the nearest thing. What you hand people tends to stay with them for years.
angles.cost_self: For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Since getting the choice right matters more to you than being on time, you let the warm moment pass. Underneath it, you want to be known as someone who truly listens.
angles.cost_others: You choose kind words as carefully as gifts. Anything plain sounds careless to you, so you choose silence rather than say something plain to someone you love. Much of your fondness goes unspoken to the very people it is for.

angles.drive: Showing how a thing is done comes more easily to you than explaining it. You trust your hands over your words, and teach by doing it next to someone rather than telling them. Learners leave you with the feel of the craft in their fingers.
angles.cost_self: Teaching by doing takes your time twice, since you would rather do a thing beside someone than write it down. You teach that way even where a note would do. Whole afternoons of your own work go to lessons a page could carry.
angles.cost_others: You teach a child by doing the whole thing yourself. Your own way is the one you know works, so you teach it rather than let them try another. The child walks away with a method that holds, learned at your side.

friction.define: As a friction, the gate stays wide open, since making is how you feel real. Your strength runs out through your hands faster than it comes back.

angles.drive: Pleasing you takes exactness. A thing has to be right in every detail before it pleases you, and you check the small part rather than enjoy the whole. You are allowed to be pleased by a thing that is nearly right.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to please costs you the pleasure. Since your pleasure has to be earned, you hold it back rather than enjoy what is only nice. You never get back an evening spent waiting to be pleased.
angles.cost_others: You look a gift over before you let it please you. You put the flaw ahead of the thanks, and keep the maker from seeing you pleased. You take from each maker the joy of having pleased you.

angles.drive: Giving is how you know you are here. The made thing in someone's hands proves you more than anything kept, so you give what you made away rather than keeping any of it. You leave yourself off the list of people you give to.
angles.cost_self: Giving too much leaves you with the least. Since keeping a thing for yourself feels mean to you, you give the best one away rather than hold on to it. With every gift, you give away a little more of your own rest.
angles.cost_others: When you love someone, you give before they ask. Giving feels more natural to you than keeping, so you hand over even the things you need. By giving it all, you leave the people you love no chance to look after you.

angles.drive: Taking it easy comes naturally to you. Because what you make comes out well without much effort, you stay with what you do well rather than learn what you do badly. While taking it easy, you leave the hard parts untried.
angles.cost_self: Your best work is what taking it easy costs you. What comes easily feels like enough, and you enjoy the version you have instead of reaching for the one beyond it. You have the better piece in you already, and only effort gets it out.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Your first try already looks right, and they see the ease without the care behind it. You teach them to aim no higher than what you settle for.

edge.lead: Metal runs through your health, your family and your career. It is the slow morning you give its whole length, the thing you made by hand that stays in the family, and the care in your work that shows before it gets named.

angles.drive: A finished thing gives you a calm that starting never does. Since a half-done piece sits with you like an open promise, you finish one thing properly rather than start three. The things you make arrive whole, every edge seen to.
angles.cost_self: Finishing comes before enjoying for you. A thing is not yours to like until it is done, and you finish the gift before the pleasure of making it. The best part of the work goes by while your mind waits for the end.
angles.cost_others: Every gift you give, you finish alone. The making feels like part of you, so you finish it yourself rather than with the person it is for. The one it is for gets your polish and misses the hours behind it.

$provenance.replaced: Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Because your first try looks finished, you show them stopping rather than pushing, and hand them good enough as the ceiling. You teach them to aim no higher than what you settle for.

angles.drive: You love the craft for its own sake, whatever the thing you are making. Shaping something with care is where you feel most at home, and the hours pass without your counting them. What you make shows that it was enjoyed in the making.
angles.cost_self: Loving the craft draws you back to the work above almost anything else. You need part of every day to go into making something, and other plans wait their turn. Friends and sleep get whatever evenings the craft leaves over.
angles.cost_others: The people around you often find you deep in a piece of work. Losing yourself in the making is your favourite way to be, and a question from the doorway takes a moment to reach you. Your family shares you with the craft.
